analysis: Examined both base-text units of docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (lines 1307-2138). The PR's only change is a documentation edit around head lines 676-684, which lies outside the supplied base excerpts. It rewords how the joining Mac's wait ends on a stop: a stop count carried in the leading Mac's status replaces the earlier 20-second "Stopped" heuristic. The supplied units are unchanged surrounding context covering the relay 503 behavior, GPU-limit planning (TB-014/T-062), prefix cache and SSD tier (T-041), update/rollback, solo vs pair, leave/uninstall and pairing-again flows. The edit is docs-only, with no code, permission, crypto or endpoint changes. It does describe an apparent behavior change: the joining Mac now treats a stop count from the leader's status, not a 20s "Stopped" reading, as a stop. The security-relevant assumption is that this count is read over the authenticated paired cable channel. The leading Mac's status is peer-supplied, so a stale or forged count could only end a wait (availability, A-018), and nothing in the supplied evidence shows this is unauthenticated or a regression. The provider-side implementation is not in this batch, so I could not verify it. No threat model entries need updating from the visible text. The doc's statements about SSD records and cache partitioning (per-tenant scope, native vs balanced precision) are consistent with T-041 (HMAC lookup tags, scope-folded keys, 30-minute TTL). No findings.
